title: Oct 24 Results: Sometimes the Cards Just Don't Fall Your Way
summary: Oct 24 brought a humbling 0-1 night. I've been around long enough to know these happen.

content.value:
## The Night That Was

Look, I've been covering this game long enough to know that some nights just don't go your way. October 24th was one of those nights—a clean 0-for-1 that stings a bit, but also reminds you why baseball remains the most humbling sport on the planet. We had one game on the slate, backed the Rays at 52%, and Milwaukee had other ideas.

## The Miss: Rays @ Brewers

We liked Tampa Bay in this one, though admittedly it was about as close to a coin flip as you'll see—52% confidence. When you're splitting hairs like that, you're essentially saying 'this could go either way,' and boy, did it ever go the other way. The Brewers took care of business at home, and our Rays pick went down in flames.

Here's the thing about October baseball that I've learned over three decades: momentum is real, home field matters more than the regular season, and sometimes the team that looks better on paper just doesn't execute. That 52% told you everything you needed to know—this was never a lock.

## The Bigger Picture

One game, one loss. It happens. I've seen hot streaks that make you feel invincible and cold snaps that make you question everything you know about the sport. The key is not letting either define you. We'll review the data, see what we might have missed in the matchup analysis, and move forward.

The beauty and curse of a single-game slate? There's nowhere to hide. Your record is your record. Tonight it's 0-1, and that's baseball.

content.title: 🔮 Tomorrow's Slate
content.sub: A rare day off to reset and prepare for what's ahead

content.value:
## What's Next

No games tomorrow means a chance to take a breath, reset the mental approach, and dive deep into the upcoming matchups. I've always believed these quiet days in the schedule are gifts—time to sharpen the analysis, review what's working and what isn't, and come back stronger.

We'll be back soon with fresh picks and hopefully better results. That's the promise of this game: there's always another day, another pitch, another chance to get it right.

author: Max
